# Book fixtures (PDF slices)

Small page-slices of real textbooks, committed so tests and gold data reuse
them without re-downloading the full (1–100 MB) source PDFs. Every fixture
is a slice cut from an openly available source PDF with `pypdfium2`
(`PdfDocument.import_pages`).

Two consumers:

- **Gold sets** — `data/gold/corrector/index.json` and
  `data/gold/extractor/index.json` reference `source_pdf:
  tests/fixtures/books/<fixture>.pdf`; the gold integrity tests
  (`tests/test_gold_corrector.py`) read through them. The corrector gold
  uses every fixture below; the extractor gold samples the algebra/analysis
  books.
- **Exercise-layer stress tests** — the six exercise slices (the algebra,
  calculus, analysis, and linear-algebra fixtures) were cut specifically to
  stress the splitter / instruction-finder / instruction-distributor logic:
  coverage spans elementary drill (dense shared lead-ins) through
  advanced-undergraduate / graduate proof exercises (mostly self-contained,
  no lead-ins) — the two ends of the exercise-governance spectrum.

Page columns: the original six give the **0-based source-PDF indices** as
cut; the newer six give **printed folio ranges** (the page numbers shown in
the book's own footer, which differ from source-PDF indices by front-matter
offset). Gold records' `page` fields are *fixture-relative*.

| Fixture | Source | Level | Pages | Why it's here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ea2e_ch1_review.pdf` | OpenStax *Elementary Algebra 2e* | elementary | src 186–188 | Chapter-1 **Review**: many short "**In** the following exercises, …" lead-ins, each governing 2–6 numbered exercises before the next lead-in, with sub-section headers interleaved. Over-extension adversarial case for the **distributor**. |
| `ea2e_sec1_3_exercises.pdf` | OpenStax *Elementary Algebra 2e* | elementary | src 69–70 | A full **section exercise set** (§1.3) plus an **"Everyday Math"** block whose word problems carry their **own embedded directive** ("Use integers to write …"). Distributor must NOT treat those as run-governing lead-ins. |
| `calc3_gradients_exercises.pdf` | OpenStax *Calculus Volume 3* | adv. undergrad | src 392–393 | Multivariable/vector calc (gradients, directional derivatives). Uses the **"For** the following exercises, …" lead-in phrasing (a different wording from the algebra books) with `[T]` technology exercises interleaved between governed runs. |
| `lebl_realanalysis_sec2_1_exercises.pdf` | Lebl *Basic Analysis I* | adv. undergrad / grad | src 58–59 | Real analysis (sequences/limits). Every item is a **self-contained** "Exercise 2.1.8: Show that …" — **no shared lead-ins**. False-positive test: splitter must not tag proof exercises as lead-ins; distributor should stamp **nothing**. |
| `lebl2_metricspaces_sec8_1_exercises.pdf` | Lebl *Basic Analysis II* | graduate | src 17–18 | Metric spaces / vector spaces of functions (linear operators, dimension). Self-contained "Exercise 8.1.6: Show that L is a linear operator." — graduate proof style, same no-lead-in stress as Lebl I on harder content. |
| `hefferon_linsys_exercises.pdf` | Hefferon *Linear Algebra* | adv. undergrad | src 42–43 | Linear systems. Self-contained exercises numbered "3.14, 3.15, …", each carrying its **own per-exercise imperative** ("Solve each system.", "Is the given vector in the set generated by …") and many flagged with a **"✓/X" recommended glyph**. Tests the splitter's rule that an own-numbered exercise with its own directive is an EXERCISE, never a lead-in — a distinct *instruction type* (per-exercise directive vs shared lead-in). |
| `combinatorics_levin.pdf` | Levin *Discrete Mathematics: An Open Introduction* | undergrad | printed 106–109 | Graph theory (isomorphisms, the Petersen graph). Two-column tables and footnotes: the corrector gold exercises footnote-routing-to-footer and table transcription. |
| `logic_hammack_truthtables.pdf` | Hammack *Book of Proof* | intro proofs | printed 47–50 | **Biconditionals and truth tables** — dense `⇔`/`⇒` symbol runs and truth-table layouts for OCR symbol fidelity. ⚠️ licence, see below. |
| `nt_stein_congruences.pdf` | Stein *Elementary Number Theory* | adv. undergrad | printed 39–42 | Structure of `(Z/pZ)*`, Mersenne primes, **Sage sessions with code + output** (the gold's `presence` errors came from `R.<x>` misread as HTML tags). ⚠️ licence, see below. |
| `ode_lebl_diffyqs.pdf` | Lebl *Notes on Diffy Qs* | undergrad | printed 29–32 | **Slope fields** with embedded figures, display math, and the Picard theorem discussion. The corrector gold's perturbed records inject polarity/substitution errors into the equations here. |
| `prob_grinstead_snell.pdf` | Grinstead & Snell *Introduction to Probability* | undergrad | printed 17–21 | Simulation of discrete probabilities, narrative prose with inline math and tables — a probability-table layout beyond the algebra books. |
| `topology_morris.pdf` | Morris *Topology without Tears* | undergrad | printed 42–45 | Topological spaces, inverse images, the finite-closed topology. Proof-style prose (`Proof.` misread as an H1 in the gold) and exercise lists. ⚠️ licence, see below. |

## Sources & licences

The original six are from works whose licences permit redistribution of
excerpts (attribution / share-alike families), and the sources were chosen
on that basis. **Three of the newer six do not satisfy that policy** — they
were added for the corrector gold without a licence re-check, and are
flagged ⚠️ above. They should be re-sliced from openly licensed
alternatives when time allows; until then their status is explicit:

- **OpenStax** *Elementary Algebra 2e*, *Calculus Volume 3* — © Rice University,
  **CC BY 4.0**.
  - https://openstax.org/details/books/elementary-algebra-2e
  - https://openstax.org/details/books/calculus-volume-3
  - PDFs under `https://assets.openstax.org/oscms-prodcms/media/documents/`
- **Jiří Lebl**, *Basic Analysis: Introduction to Real Analysis*, Vol. I & II,
  and *Notes on Diffy Qs* — dual **CC BY-SA 4.0** / CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
  https://www.jirka.org/ra/ (Vol I `realanal.pdf`, Vol II `realanal2.pdf`),
  https://www.jirka.org/diffyqs/
- **Jim Hefferon**, *Linear Algebra* — **CC BY-SA 3.0** (also GFDL).
  https://hefferon.net/linearalgebra/ (book PDF at
  `https://jheffero.w3.uvm.edu/linearalgebra/book.pdf`).
- **Oscar Levin**, *Discrete Mathematics: An Open Introduction* — **CC BY-SA
  4.0** (editions 1–3; the 4th edition moved to CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
  https://discrete.openmathbooks.org/
- **Charles Grinstead & J. Laurie Snell**, *Introduction to Probability*
  (AMS, 2nd ed.) — **GNU Free Documentation License (GFDL)**.
  https://chance.dartmouth.edu/teaching_aids/books_articles/probability_book/book.html

### ⚠️ Licence exceptions (do not extend)

- **`logic_hammack_truthtables.pdf`** — Hammack, *Book of Proof*, is
  **CC BY-NC-ND 4.0**. The ND term forbids derivative redistribution, which
  this repo's policy excludes ("NoDerivs … makes redistributing excerpts
  unsafe" — see `data/gold/extractor/README.md`, which deliberately excluded
  Hammack from the extractor set for exactly this reason). The corrector
  gold nonetheless uses it; the contradiction is known and unresolved.
- **`nt_stein_congruences.pdf`** — Stein, *Elementary Number Theory*, is
  **not open-licensed**: Springer © 2009, distributed as a free PDF for
  personal/classroom use, with print-distribution rights reserved. Slicing
  and committing excerpts exceeds that grant as written.
- **`topology_morris.pdf`** — Morris, *Topology without Tears*, is
  **all-rights-reserved** ("No part of this book may be reproduced by any
  process without prior written permission from the author"); the PDF is
  free to download but not libre.

> Note: Treil, *Linear Algebra Done Wrong* was evaluated but **excluded** — it is
> CC BY-NC-**ND**, whose NoDerivs term makes redistributing excerpts unsafe.

## `test.pdf` — scratch file, do not use

`test.pdf` (18 pages, ~5.4 MB, "CLICK HERE VIEW ALL SOLUTIONS") is an
unreferenced leftover — nothing in `src/`, `tests/`, or `data/gold/`
points at it. It should be deleted; it carries no provenance and does not
belong in the fixture set.

## Re-slicing / adding fixtures

```python
import pypdfium2 as p
src = p.PdfDocument("elementary-algebra-2e_-_WEB.pdf")   # full download, not committed
out = p.PdfDocument.new()
out.import_pages(src, [186, 187, 188])                    # 0-based page indices
out.save("tests/fixtures/books/ea2e_ch1_review.pdf")
```

To find good pages in a fresh book, scan page text for the lead-in phrase
(`in the following exercises` / `for the following exercises`, case-insensitive)
and rank by count; for proof-style books, count `Exercise \d+\.\d+\.\d+`
occurrences per page to find dense section-end exercise blocks.

**Before adding a fixture, verify the source licence permits excerpt
redistribution** (attribution / share-alike / GFDL families; no ND, no
"free to read" grants that stop at redistribution) — the three exceptions
above are the cost of skipping that step.
